decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 2.25% to 2.5%. The vote was 10-0.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity rose at a solid rate.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January indicates that the labor market remains strong but that growth of economic activity …”

changes.quote: Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Payroll employment was little changed in February, but job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.”

changes.quote: Growth of household spending and business fixed investment slowed in the first quarter.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Recent indicators point to slower growth of household spending and business fixed investment in the first quarter.”

changes.quote: On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have declined and are running below 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “On a 12-month basis, overall inflation has declined, largely as a result of lower energy prices; inflation for items other than food and energy remains near 2 p…”

changes.quote: Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Richard H. Clarida; Charles L. Evans; Esther L. George; Randal K. Quarles; and Eric S. Rosengren.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; John C. Williams, Vice Chairman; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; …”

tone_quotes.quote: Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have declined and are running below 2 percent.

This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.73% APR costs about $61.38 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.52% and moved +1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.17% would rise by about $1.75 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.8%, and employers added an average of 162k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.9% over the past year (March 2019); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +4 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.75%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.28% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 98%, cut 0%, hike 2%.

citations.detail: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent.
